Title: Bored Piles
QS_NOTE: Piling is substructure measured in linear metres so billing it under 5 In-situ concrete (which measures concrete volume/formwork/reinforcement) mismatches the row's own 'm' unit; 4 Foundations is the nearest home because this scheme has no Piling section (NRM2 7) - see report caveat about the out-of-scope bare-foundation fallback which is also 5.

Title: Shoring and Underpinning
QS_NOTE: Underpinning and permanent sheet piling are substructure work so 4 Foundations is right; note the rule also catches temporary shoring which is a Division 01 / preliminaries item and a QS may want that split out rather than billed as permanent work.

Title: Driven Piles
QS_NOTE: Same reasoning as row 109 - driven piling is foundation work not superstructure in-situ concrete; moved to 4 Foundations for consistency with the bored-pile row.

Title: Driven Piles
QS_NOTE: Precast-material twin of row 111 and must move with it or a precast pile bills under a different section than an identical in-situ one.

Title: Fences and Gates
QS_NOTE: Fences and gates bill under the new 41 Fencing, gates and barriers; previously 4 Foundations because the scheme had no external-works section.

Title: Earth Moving
QS_NOTE: Bulk earth moving is excavating and filling which this scheme calls 3 Groundworks; 3 exists in the vocabulary but appears on no row in the map so it cannot be written here without being added first.

Title: Earth Moving
QS_NOTE: Same as row 131 - a toposolid cut/fill volume is groundworks (3) not foundations; code 3 is unused in the map.

Title: Grading
QS_NOTE: Grading and formation levels are groundworks (3) not foundations; code 3 is unused in the map.

Title: Excavation and Fill
QS_NOTE: A Revit building pad is excavation and filling which is groundworks (3); foundation excavation still measures under groundworks in NRM2 rather than under the Foundations heading; code 3 is unused in the map.

Title: Erosion and Sedimentation Controls
QS_NOTE: Erosion and sedimentation controls are CSI 31 25 00 site preparation, and both halves of the rule (temporary silt fence, permanent swale) are site-preparation works, so 3 Groundworks covers the row without splitting it. The temporary/permanent distinction would matter for a preliminaries section, which this scheme does not have.

Title: Concrete Paving
QS_NOTE: Rigid (concrete) paving is external works; new section 40.

Title: Asphalt Paving
QS_NOTE: Flexible (asphalt) road construction is external works; new section 40.

Title: Pavement Markings
QS_NOTE: Pavement markings are measured with the paving they are applied to; 40.

Title: Asphalt Paving
QS_NOTE: Car park paving is external works; 40.

Title: Unit Paving
QS_NOTE: External unit paving to footways and plazas is external works, not an internal floor finish; 40.

Title: Concrete Curbs and Gutters
QS_NOTE: Kerbs, channels and gutters are measured with the road works; 40.

Title: Retaining Walls
QS_NOTE: A retaining wall is a permanent structural wall and this file's stated convention bills every wall at 14 (its header notes 03 30 00 is 5 for a concrete floor and 14 for a concrete wall); 'Foundations' is wrong - flagged as a judgement call since a mass concrete retaining wall could equally be argued to 5.

Title: Fences and Gates
QS_NOTE: Rule split: it matched fence|gate|balustrade and could not resolve to one section. Narrowed to fence|gate here, billing under the new 41 Fencing, gates and barriers; a balustrade is a railing and now has its own appended rule at 05 52 00 Metal Railings / 20.

Title: Site Furnishings
QS_NOTE: Site furnishings are furniture and fittings and this map already bills benches and seating at 22 (Specialty Equipment bench|pew|seating); NRM2 proper puts external fixtures at 38 but that has no code here and 22 is the established internal precedent.

Title: Site Improvements
QS_NOTE: General site improvements are external works; 40.

Title: Site Improvements
QS_NOTE: Entourage is Revit presentation context and should generate NO priced line at all. That is now enforced where it belongs -- OST_Entourage is in the takeoff exclusion set -- so this code is never reached; it is set to 40 only so the map does not claim external works are foundations.

Title: Trees
QS_NOTE: Tree planting is soft landscaping; new section 42.

Title: Turf and Grasses
QS_NOTE: Turfing and seeding are soft landscaping; 42.

Title: Plants
QS_NOTE: Shrub and plant beds are soft landscaping; 42.

Title: Planting Irrigation
QS_NOTE: Irrigation mains and laterals are a piped water supply system so 32 Piped supply systems is the right home and matches every other water-carrying pipe row in this map; a QS whose landscape contractor prices irrigation as part of soft landscaping may prefer it there instead.

Title: Planting Irrigation
QS_NOTE: Landscape irrigation heads sit on the piped supply system so 32 is correct; this row's real job is diverting them away from the Sprinklers category default of 36 fire suppression which it still does.

Title: Water Utility Distribution Piping
QS_NOTE: Buried site water distribution main is a piped supply system so 32 is correct and consistent with the in-building DCW row; the trench excavation and backfill is groundworks but that is measured separately and is not this row's element.

Title: Natural-Gas Distribution
QS_NOTE: Left at 33 only to stay consistent with the in-building gas row (23 11 23) which is also 33 - but gas is arguably 32 Piped supply systems rather than Mechanical services and if the QS moves this row the in-building row must move with it; genuinely uncertain.

Title: Sanitary Utility Sewerage Piping
QS_NOTE: Below-ground foul drainage is NOT a piped supply system - this scheme has an exactly correct code 31 Drainage below ground but no row in the map uses it so it cannot be written here; add 31 to the map first.

Title: Storm Utility Drainage Piping
QS_NOTE: Below-ground surface-water drainage belongs at 31 Drainage below ground not 32 Piped supply systems; code 31 exists in the vocabulary but is unused in the map.

Title: Subdrainage
QS_NOTE: Subsoil and land drainage belongs at 31 Drainage below ground not 32 Piped supply systems; code 31 exists in the vocabulary but is unused in the map.

Title: Electrical Utility Transmission and Distribution
QS_NOTE: Buried site electrical distribution is still electrical services so 34 is correct and consistent with the in-building Conduits row; the duct trench excavation is groundworks but is measured separately.

Title: Sanitary Utility Sewerage Structures
QS_NOTE: Manholes and inspection chambers are measured with below-ground drainage (31) not as a piped supply system; code 31 exists in the vocabulary but is unused in the map.

Title: Storm Utility Water Drains
QS_NOTE: Soakaways gullies and catchpits are below-ground drainage ancillaries (31) not piped supply; code 31 exists in the vocabulary but is unused in the map.

Title: Utility Septic Tanks
QS_NOTE: Septic tanks are measured with below-ground drainage (31) alongside the drain runs they serve not as a piped supply system; code 31 exists in the vocabulary but is unused in the map.

Title: Water Utility Storage Tanks
QS_NOTE: A potable water storage tank is part of the piped supply installation so 32 is right; if the 'reservoir' alternative catches a site-built concrete structure its shell would be in-situ concrete (5) with only the pipework and fittings at 32.

Title: Sanitary Sewerage Utilities
QS_NOTE: A packaged sewage treatment plant is measured with below-ground drainage (31) as a drainage installation not as a piped supply system; some QSs bill packaged plant as mechanical plant (33) instead so this is a judgement - either way 32 is the weakest of the three; code 31 is unused in the map.
